decision.explanation: The transformation gives y₁=x₁−x₂ and y₂=x₁, so x₁=y₂ and x₂=y₂−y₁. Thus Q(x)=(x₁+x₂)²=(2y₂−y₁)²=y₁²−4y₁y₂+4y₂².

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & ={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+-2{y}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}^{2}+{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Given that [y1y2]=[1−110][x1x2], express the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+2x1x2+x22 in terms of the components of y.

a
y12−2y1y2+2y22
b
y12+2y1y2+2y22
c
y12−2y1y2+y22
d
y12−6y1y2+y22
e
y12−4y1y2+4y22
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[y1y2]=[1−110][x1x2]

gives the following expressions for y1 and y2:

y1=x1−x2y2=x1

By solving the second equation for x1 and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for x1 and x2:

x1=y2x2=−y1+y2

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

Q(x)=x12+2x1x2+x22=y22+2y2(−y1+y2)+(−y1+y2)2=y22+−2y2y1+2y22+y12−2y2y2+y22=y12−4y1y2+4y22

content.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2} & ={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the second equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the first equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+(-{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{2}^{2}+-2{y}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}^{2}+{y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{2}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 \\ 5 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-1 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & \,-1 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & \,-1 \\ \,\,-1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\,4 & 2 \\ 1 & \,\,1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24 & 10 \\ 10 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

 express the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}$ in terms of the components of $y.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

gives the following expressions for ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

By solving the first equation for ${x}_{1}$ and substituting it into the second equation, we obtain the following expressions for ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{y}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} & =-{y}_{1}-{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(-{y}_{1})^{2}-4(-{y}_{1})(-{y}_{1}-{y}_{2})+2(-{y}_{1}-{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+2{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-{y}_{1}^{2}+2{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
